segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Eighteen. In any triangle, the greater side subtends the greater angle. Given triangle A B C with side A C greater than side A B, we prove that angle A B C is greater than angle B C A.

segments.text: Since side A C is greater than A B, cut off segment A D from A C equal to A B. Then construct segment B D.

subsegments.text: Since side A C is greater than A B, cut off segment A D from A C equal to A B. Then construct segment B D.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since angle A D B is an exterior angle of triangle B C D, it is greater than the interior and opposite angle D C B. Yet because A B equals A D in isosceles triangle A B D, base angle A D B equals angle A B D, so angle A B D is also greater than angle A C B. Since the whole angle A B C is greater than its part A B D, angle A B C is much greater than angle B C A, as was required to prove.
